item.title: Summer music highlights of 2026
item.description: Summer is the time to enjoy live music, indoors and out. Scroll through our gallery of some of 2026's leading musical acts, featuring images by CBS News photojournalist Jake Barlow and photographers Ed Spinelli and Kirstine Walton.

item.title: Saudi Arabia's MBS told Trump to strike Houthis in Yemen, sources say
item.description: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman personally pressed President Trump to take military action against the Iran-backed Houthis as the group advanced rapidly along Yemen's Red Sea coast, two sources say. CBS News' Natalie Brand, Aaron MacLean and Chris Livesay have more.

item.title: Fed rate hike likelihood jumps to nearly 90% after hotter CPI report
item.description: Investors believe the Fed will raise borrowing costs as it works to tame inflation, which has risen a full percentage point since the Iran war started.

item.title: Ross Fire still burning, with over 90,000 acres scorched
item.description: The wildfire, which has torn through Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forced evacuations, closed roads and disrupted schools.

item.title: Diesel hits record $6 a gallon as Houthis take key Red Sea territory

item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said there is no longer a risk of people getting sick with cyclosporiasis from this outbreak and is confident that all related iceberg lettuce is off the market.

item.description: The calls from your credit card issuer may have stopped, but that silence may not mean what you think it does.

item.title: Priest shares how Trinity Church gave "amazing grace" to weary 9/11 recovery workers
item.description: New York City's Trinity Church became a hub of activity and a place of respite for first responders and recovery workers following the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. Father Michael Bird shares the church's story.

item.title: Watch: Trump remarks on 9/11 at the Pentagon 25 years since terrorist attacks
item.description: President Trump delivered remarks commemorating the September 11, 2001, terror attacks 25 years since they occurred. Mr. Trump addressed a crowd at the Pentagon, where hijackers crashed American Airlines Flight 77.

item.title: Watch: Third and fourth moment of silence in NYC and timeline of 9/11 attacks
item.description: At 9:59 a.m. ET on Sept. 11, 2001, the South Tower collapsed at the World Trade Center in New York City during a series of terrorist attacks that changed the U.S. forever. At 10:03 a.m. ET, the passengers on United Airlines Flight 93 launched a counterattack on the hijackers aboard their plane, causing a crash into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania. It's believed the aircraft may have been headed toward Washington, D.C.

item.title: How Americans aboard Flight 93 that crashed in Shanksville on 9/11 decided to fight terrorists back
item.description: The passengers aboard United Airlines Flight 93 made 37 phone calls to loved ones minutes before their plane crashed in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, on September 11, 2001. Those aboard the plane made the decision to launch a counterattack on the hijackers, possibly preventing another massive strike against the U.S.

item.title: Afghan woman dubbed an "alien terrorist" deported in obscure court's first case
item.description: An Afghan permanent resident living in Texas has been deported after the Justice Department accused her of being an "alien terrorist," in the first such case of its kind.

item.title: Man buried alive under 30 feet of rubble on 9/11 recalls being found in NYC at Ground Zero
item.description: Will Jimeno, a rookie Port Authority police officer, rushed to the World Trade Center to help save lives on Sept. 11, 2001. He was found after being buried alive under 30 feet of rubble when the South Tower suddenly began to collapse above him.

item.title: Sweden's election could mark major milestone for Europe's populist right
item.description: Once shunned over its extremist roots, the Sweden Democrats could enter government for the first time as voters weigh immigration, crime and Sweden's political transformation.

item.title: Gen. Dan Caine remembers 9/11 and getting orders to shoot down planes threatening D.C.
item.description: Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Gen. Dan Caine, remembers being an Air Force major on Sep. 11, 2001, and being one of four pilots ordered to shoot down any plane that may threaten Washington, D.C.

item.description: One of the women told police that she took the job for the money and because "I was attracted by the fact I could go to Japan for free," Nippon TV reported.
